items.title: A morphism of algebraic spaces is finite exactly when it is affine and proper

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, finiteness is equivalent to being affine and proper (source lines 9486-9494). The proof notes that in both cases the morphism is representable and the conditions may be checked after base change to an affine scheme mapping into Y, invoking the locality statements for integrality, affineness and properness, and then applies the corresponding equivalence for morphisms of schemes.
